title: Vallée's diaries keep pointing to the Carlyle Group
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Vallée's diaries keep pointing to the Carlyle Group, about unspecified at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Oh yeah. So like you read Jock Valet's diaries, you know, he he publishes his diaries, Forbidden Science volumes 1 through five. And I think it's like three or volume three or four. He always has lunch with all these people and you know these like spooky insider types and they're constantly like look at the Carile group
think like uh because Carile Group has a lot of defense interests right? It's this multinational conglomerate. Do you think there's anything to the jock valet theory
tellings.difference: Calls it Vallée's theory and stresses Carlyle's multinational defense interests, without citing the diaries' lunch conversations.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the claim, drawn from Vallée, that the Carlyle Group is tied to the UFO secret. This telling frames it as Vallée's theory and points to Carlyle's defense interests.

as_told.title: Vallee theory and Carlyle Group defense interests

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the published diaries of the UFO researcher Jacques Vallee, a five-volume set called Forbidden Science, Vallee keeps having lunch with secretive insider types who tell him to look at the Carlyle Group, which Michels describes as a multinational conglomerate with big defense interests. Michels asks his guest whether there is anything to this idea, which would mean a private company with defense ties sits close to the UFO secret.
